Exhibit 99.1

 

Boxlight Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Gross Margin Expands to 37.1%, Net Loss Narrows to $1.0 Million and Adjusted EBITDA Improves to $2.4 Million

 

Duluth, GA – Business Wire – November 17, 2026 – Boxlight Corporation (Nasdaq: BOXL) (“Boxlight” or the “Company”), a leading provider of interactive technology solutions, today announced the Company’s financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

 

Financial and Operational Highlights:

 

 

•

Revenue was $30.1 million for the quarter, an increase of 2.5% from the prior year quarter

 

•

Gross profit margin in the third quarter of 2026 improved 800 basis points to 37.1% from 29.1% in the prior year quarter

 

•

Net loss was $1.0 million, an 83.5% improvement from $6.2 million in the prior year quarter

 

•

Net loss per basic and diluted common share was $1.78, compared to $67.65 in the prior year quarter

 

•

Adjusted EBITDA1 improved by $2.8 million on a constant currency basis to $2.4 million from the prior year quarter

 

•

Reduced senior secured term loan by approximately $2.3 million to $30.0 million

 

•

Ended the quarter with $6.3 million in cash

 

•

Closed $7.5 million Series D Convertible Preferred Stock private placement, with $5.5 million funded, and the remaining $2 million expected to be funded in the fourth quarter, subject to the effectiveness of the Company's resale registration statement and other applicable conditions

 

•

Closed $850,000 Series E Convertible Preferred Stock private placement in the third quarter resulting in an additional $0.4 million repayment in WhiteHawk debt principal in October 2026

 

•

Entered into an equity line of credit providing access to up to $15 million of capital over 36 months

 

•

Clevertouch® gained market share to become the No. 4 interactive display brand in North America and No. 5 in EMEA, according to Futuresource Consulting

 

•

Launched Clevertouch Focus, an EDLA-certified interactive display that connects teaching, campus communication and school safety

 

•

Introduced Boxlight Composer, a platform that helps resellers design, install and verify Symphony campus communication deployments at scale

 

•

Earned six Tech & Learning Awards of Excellence: Back to School 2026 for Symphony, the Symphonic Series and Clevertouch Focus

 

Management Commentary 

 

“Our third quarter 2026 results show meaningful improvement across our business,” said Jennifer Grabow, Interim Chief Financial Officer. “Revenue grew to $30.1 million, gross margin improved to 37.1%, net loss narrowed to $1.0 million from $6.2 million and Adjusted EBITDA increased by $2.8 million to $2.4 million. This improvement is the result of deliberate actions to strengthen gross margin and reduce operating expenses across the company.”

 

“We have also strengthened our balance sheet,” Ms. Grabow added. “We raised $5.5 million of the $7.5 million Series D financing, added a $15 million equity line and reduced our senior secured term loan to $30.0 million. At the same time, Clevertouch gained share to become the No. 4 interactive display brand in North America and No. 5 in EMEA, according to Futuresource Consulting, and our Symphony platform is extending our reach into campus communication and school safety. As schools begin replacing aging classroom displays and other legacy technology, we believe Boxlight is well positioned for growth in 2027 and beyond.”

1

 

Financial Results for the Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 vs. the Three Months Ended September 30, 2025

 

Total revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $30.1 million as compared to $29.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, resulting in a 2.5% increase. The increase in revenues was driven by higher sales volume compared to the prior year quarter, reflecting higher global demand for interactive flat panel displays.

 

Cost of revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $18.9 million as compared to $20.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, resulting in a 9.1% decrease. The decrease in cost of revenues was primarily attributable to the normalized tariff rates in 2026 as compared to higher tariff rates in 2025.


Gross profit for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $11.2 million as compared to $8.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of 30.7%. Gross profit margin was 37.1% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 29.1% for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in gross profit margin was primarily driven by the impact of normalized tariffs in the current year along with the increase in sales.

 

General and administrative expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $7.9 million, representing 26.3% of revenue as compared to $8.7 million representing 29.8% of revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in general and administrative expenses for the period ended September 30, 2026 was due to decreases of $0.3 million in professional fees, $0.2 million in credit loss expenses, $0.2 million in contract and consulting expenses, and a $0.1 million decrease in sales and marketing expenses.

 

Depreciation and amortization expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $2.5 million, representing 8.4% of revenue as compared to $2.6 million representing 9.0% of revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2025.


Research and development expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 were $0.9 million and $1.1 million, respectively and represented 3.1% and 3.8% of revenue, respectively. Research and development expense primarily consists of costs associated with the development of proprietary technology. The decrease was attributable to the streamlining of research and development expenses.

 

Other expense, net for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $1.0 million as compared to $2.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, representing a decrease of $1.5 million. The decrease in other expense was primarily driven by a $1.7 million decrease in interest expense on our term loan, a $0.4 million decrease in losses from change in fair value of derivative liability, and a $0.3 million decrease in losses from change in fair value of common warrants offset by an increase in other expense of $0.9 million.

 

Net loss decreased $5.2 million to $1.0 million and was a result of the changes noted above. Net loss attributable to common shareholders was $1.3 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $6.5 million in the third quarter of last year, after deducting fixed dividends (recorded but not paid) for Series B preferred shareholders of approximately $0.3 million in both years.

 

Total comprehensive loss was $1.1 million for the third quarter of 2026 compared to $6.1 million for the third quarter of 2025, reflecting the effect of cumulative foreign currency translation adjustments on consolidation, with the net effect of a $(48) thousand loss and a $134 thousand gain for the third quarter of 2026 and 2025, respectively.

 

Basic and diluted loss per share for the third quarter of 2026 was $1.78 compared to $67.65 per basic and diluted share for the third quarter of last year.

 

EBITDA2, a non-GAAP measure, for the third quarter of 2026 was $2.4 million, as compared to $(1.1) million EBITDA for the third quarter of last year.

 

Adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026 was $2.4 million, as compared to $(0.4) million in the third quarter of 2025. Adjustments to EBITDA included changes in fair value of common warrants, stock-based compensation expense, gains/losses from the remeasurement of derivative liabilities, severance charges, and the effects of purchase accounting adjustments in connection with prior period acquisitions.

2

 

Financial Results for the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026 (3Q26 YTD) vs. the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2025 (3Q25 YTD)

 

Total revenues for 3Q26 YTD were $78.4 million as compared to $82.6 million for 3Q25 YTD, resulting in a 5.1% decrease. The decrease in revenues was driven by lower sales volume in the audio segment.

 

Cost of revenues for 3Q26 YTD was $47.4 million as compared to $55.2 million for 3Q25 YTD, resulting in a 14.2% decrease. The decrease in cost of revenues was attributable to the decrease in units sold offset by the favorable savings from normalized tariff rates and a $2.8 million tariff refund.

 

Gross profit for 3Q26 YTD was $31.0 million as compared to $27.4 million for 3Q25 YTD. Gross profit margin improved to 39.5% for 3Q26 YTD compared to 33.1% for 3Q25 YTD, primarily driven by the $2.8 million in tariff refunds, which reduced current year cost of revenues.

 

General and administrative expense for 3Q26 YTD was $24.6 million and 31.4% of revenue, as compared to $27.3 million and 33.0% of revenue for 3Q25 YTD. The decrease in general and administrative expenses for the period ended September 30, 2026 was due to decreases of $0.8 million in employee related expenses, $0.7 million in contract and consulting expenses, $0.3 million in professional fee expenses, $0.2 million in sales and marketing expenses, $0.2 million in stock compensation expense, $0.2 million in occupancy expenses, and a $0.2 million decrease in bad debt expense.


Depreciation and amortization expenses for 3Q26 YTD were $7.7 million, representing 9.8% of revenue as compared to $7.7 million representing 9.3% of revenue for 3Q25 YTD.

 

Research and development expense was $2.8 million or 3.6% of revenue for 3Q26 YTD as compared to $3.2 million or 3.8% of revenue for 3Q25 YTD. Research and development expense primarily consists of costs associated with the development of proprietary technology. The decrease was attributable to the streamlining of research and development expenses.

 

Other expense for 3Q26 YTD was $3.8 million as compared to $3.5 million for 3Q25 YTD, representing an increase of $0.3 million. The increase in other expense reflected decrease of $4.4 million in interest expense on our term loan, $0.3 million in losses from change in fair value of derivative liability, and $0.6 million in loss on warrant issuance more than offset by a $4.2 million increase in other expense, net, and a $1.4 million decrease in gains from change in fair value of common warrants.

 

Net loss attributable to common shareholders was $(8.0) million and $(15.1) million for 3Q26 YTD and 3Q25 YTD, respectively, after deducting fixed dividends (recorded but not paid) for Series B preferred shareholders of $1.0 million in each year.

 

Basic and diluted loss per share for 3Q26 YTD was $ (12.48) per basic and diluted share, compared to $ (175.48) per basic and diluted share for 3Q25 YTD.

 

EBITDA3 for 3Q26 YTD was $3.2 million, as compared to $1.2 million EBITDA for 3Q25 YTD. Adjusted EBITDA for 3Q26 YTD was $3.6 million, as compared to $1.4 million for 3Q25 YTD.

3

 

Balance Sheet; Credit Agreement

 

At September 30, 2026, Boxlight had $6.3 million in cash and cash equivalents, $1.1 million in working capital and $31.7 million in debt, net of debt issuance costs. The change in net working capital was attributable to the reclassification of our term loan from long-term to short-term debt, resulting from its maturity occurring within 12 months of September 30, 2026.

 

The Company was not in compliance with its financial covenants related to the borrowing base or the Minimum Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA under the WhiteHawk Credit Agreement at September 30, 2026. The Lenders granted a limited waiver of defaults for the period ended September 30, 2026.

 

In August 2026, the Company closed the first tranche of a private placement of Series D Convertible Preferred Stock (the “Series D PIPE”) for $5.5 million in gross proceeds ($4.8 million, net of fees), entered into an equity purchase agreement with Secure Net Capital LLC for the sale of up to $15 million of Class A common stock over 36 months (the “Equity Line”), and used a portion of the proceeds to repay approximately $2.25 million of principal and $0.14 million of prepayment penalty under its WhiteHawk Credit Agreement.

 

On September 30, 2026, the Company issued 106,250 shares of Series E Convertible Preferred Stock to J.J. Astor & Co. (“JJA”), an entity affiliated with the Company’s Executive Chairman, for gross proceeds of $850,000. Amounts outstanding under the Company’s inventory finance agreement with JJA approximately $2.2 million as of November 16, 2026, the term of which was extended to November 3, 2027, are convertible into Class A common stock at JJA’s election.

 

On September 2, 2026, the Nasdaq Hearings Panel determined that the Company had regained compliance with Nasdaq’s $2.5 million Shareholders’ Equity Listing Requirement, subject to a one-year Discretionary Panel Monitor effective August 17, 2026.

 

On November 10, 2026, the Company’s stockholders approved, among other things, issuances of Class A common stock upon conversion of the Series D and Series E Preferred Stock and under the Equity Line and the JJA inventory finance agreement, issuances below the exercise price of the WhiteHawk warrant, the 2026 Equity Incentive Plan, an increase in authorized Class A common stock from 55,000,000 to 500,000,000 shares, and authority for the Board of Directors to effect one or more reverse stock splits at a ratio of up to 1-for-1,000. The Company expects to receive an additional $2 million in gross proceeds from the Series D PIPE investors in the second tranche upon effectiveness of its resale registration statement on Form S-1, and to begin utilizing the $15 million Equity Line, in each case subject to the satisfaction of applicable conditions.

 

About Boxlight Corporation

 

Boxlight Corporation (Nasdaq: BOXL) is a leading provider of education technology, campus communication and school safety solutions. Through its Clevertouch® interactive and non-interactive displays, CleverLive® digital signage, FrontRow™ classroom audio and the Boxlight Symphony™ campus communication platform, Boxlight connects instruction, communication and emergency alerting across classrooms, campuses and districts in a single integrated ecosystem. For more information, visit boxlight.com.

4

 

Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures

 

To provide investors with additional insight and allow for a more comprehensive understanding of the information used by management in its financial and decision-making surrounding pro forma operations, we supplement our consolidated financial statements presented on a basis consistent with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles, or GAAP, with EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA, which are non-GAAP financial measures of earnings. EBITDA represents net loss before income tax expense (benefit), interest expense, depreciation and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA represents EBITDA plus stock-based compensation, severance charges, the change in fair value of derivative liabilities, change in fair value of common warrants, loss on warrant issuance, purchase accounting impact of inventory markup and fair value adjustments to deferred revenue. Our management uses EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA as financial measures to evaluate the profitability and efficiency of our business model. We use these non-GAAP financial measures to assess the strength of the underlying operations of our business. These adjustments, and the non-GAAP financial measures that are derived from them, provide supplemental information to analyze our operations between periods and over time. We find this especially useful when reviewing pro forma results of operations, which include large non-cash amortizations of intangible assets from acquisitions and stock-based compensation. Investors should consider our non-GAAP financial measures in addition to, and not as a substitute for, financial measures prepared in accordance with GAAP. Non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered as an alternative to net income (loss), operating income (loss), or any other performance measures derived in accordance with GAAP.

 

We report our operating results in accordance with U.S. GAAP. We have disclosed in the table below the results on a constant currency basis to facilitate period-to-period comparisons of our results without regard to the impact of fluctuating foreign currency exchange rates. The term foreign currency exchange rates refers to the exchange rates we use to translate our operating results into U.S. Dollars for all countries where the functional currency is not the U.S. Dollar. Because we are a global company, the foreign currency exchange rates used for translation may have a significant effect on our reported results. In general, our reported financial results are affected positively by a weaker U.S. Dollar and are affected negatively by a stronger U.S. Dollar as compared to the foreign currencies in which we conduct our business. References to our operating results on a constant-currency basis mean our operating results without the impact of foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations.

 

We believe disclosure of constant-currency results is helpful to investors because it facilitates period-to-period comparisons of our results by increasing the transparency of our underlying performance by excluding the impact of fluctuating foreign currency exchange rates. However, constant-currency results are non-U.S. GAAP financial measures and are not meant to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for comparable measures prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Constant-currency results have no standardized meaning prescribed by U.S. GAAP, are not prepared under any comprehensive set of accounting rules or principles, and should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Constant-currency results have limitations in their usefulness to investors and may be calculated differently from, and therefore may not be directly comparable to, similarly titled measures used by other companies.

 

5

 

Discussion of the Effect of Constant Currency on Financial Condition 

 

We calculate constant-currency amounts by translating local currency amounts in the current period at actual foreign exchange rates for the prior year period. Our constant-currency results do not eliminate the transaction currency impact of purchases and sales of products in a currency other than the functional currency.
